tool_input.body:
## Summary

Commits the output of `ethos enable`, and records the empirical test of whether it actually fixed the trailer chain.

**It installed the hook. The hook stamps nothing.** Proven by a real commit, not inferred.

## What `enable` did

```
hook:commit-msg  installed  .beads/hooks/commit-msg
hook:pre-commit  chained    .beads/hooks/pre-commit
vendored         .punt-labs/ethos/{CLAUDE.md,ETHOS-SETUP.md,.vendored-manifest}
marker           .punt-labs/ethos/enabled
gitignore        .punt-labs/**/local/**, .punt-labs/ethos/missions/**/*.lock, .punt-labs/**/*.local.*
import           @.punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md added to CLAUDE.md
```

This is **part 3 of `xboing-yeuw`, and it was one command.** The repo had been enabled before the trailer-hook feature existed, and `enable` — documented as idempotent, *"re-running is the upgrade path"* — hadn't been re-run. "Chained" confirms ethos coexists with beads' hooks rather than contending for the single-valued `core.hooksPath`.

`ethos doctor` moves accordingly:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Audit seal hook | not enabled here | **chained seal section active** |
| Seal hook currency | no section installed | **matches this build (e7cacc3c)** |
| Trailer hook currency | no section installed | **matches this build (73b3300a)** |
| Local extension files | **WARN** no gitignore rule | **PASS** ignored and untracked |

CLAUDE.md is 142 lines after the import — inside the 200-line budget in `.claude/rules/claude-md.md`.

## The test — and the result

Mission `m-2026-09-06-009` was opened as the test vehicle. Commit `a1d7a04` was made while it was open, with the hook installed and current.

```
$ git log -2 --format='%h %s%n  trailers=[%(trailers:only,valueonly)]'
be9e122 test(ethos): ...   trailers=[]
a1d7a04 chore(ethos): ...  trailers=[]
```

**No `Mission:` trailer. No `Delegation:` trailer.**

The chain breaks *upstream* of the hook, at the session sidecar:

- creating the mission emitted, as all nine did today, `binding mission: no session in context -- active-mission sidecar not updated`
- `ethos hook commit-trailers` — the exact call the hook makes — exits 0 printing nothing
- 133 session directories hold exactly **two** `active-mission` sidecars, containing `m-2026-09-02-006` and `m-2026-08-30-014`. Neither is this session's mission; both are days stale.

## The hook is not at fault

Worth saying, because it's genuinely well built. Its own source: *"No resolvable session, no ethos on PATH, or no active mission means no trailer. The hook never guesses."* It preserves a chained host hook's exit status so chaining can't mask a host failure, gates on the enabled marker, stays idempotent against a quoted `Mission: ` in a body, falls back to plain-append rather than dropping a trailer on `mktemp`/`mv` failure, and deliberately leaves stderr unsuppressed because *"a silently missing trailer is the failure class this hook exists to prevent."* It also documents and fixes a prior cross-session attribution bug (`ethos-pobi`).

So **part 3 is done and shouldn't be redone.** `xboing-yeuw` stays open on part 2 alone.

## A correction to my own earlier claim

I wrote on `xboing-icp1` that doctor *"cannot distinguish current from absent."* Running enable disproved it — the message text distinguishes clearly. What doctor doesn't do is treat absence as a **problem**: both states are `PASS`, so an operator scanning for red sees nothing wrong. Narrower finding, narrower fix. Corrected on the bead.

Two of `xboing-icp1`'s items are resolved by enable (the gitignore WARN; both hook sections installed). Its FAIL remains — `latex-tech-architect` is still on no team, so doctor still exits 1.

## Two side effects worth knowing

1. **The seal writes into tracked files.** `enable` warned that `core.hooksPath` sits inside the work tree. Observed immediately: `a1d7a04` was staged as 8 files and landed as **20 (+1864 lines)** — the pre-commit seal swept in nine `missions/*/log-no-session-*.jsonl` and three `sessions/*/audit-*.jsonl`. Not wrong, but routine commits will now carry audit artifacts the author didn't stage.
2. **Removing a worktree loses unsealed audit lines.** Five warnings on commit: `active session <id> has no live audit file in <path>; if it was deleted, unsealed lines were lost` — three naming the `.claude/worktrees/slsa-provenance-restore` I removed earlier today. Worth knowing before the next `ExitWorktree --remove`.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (no application code changes — hooks, config, vendored guide, audit artifacts)

Not changing this one — the comment already says exactly what you're asking it to say. The quoted fragment is a parenthetical inside a sentence whose next clause covers the chained case.

`.beads/hooks/pre-commit:35-37`, in full:

> Exit status on the non-failure paths (success, nothing-to-seal, gitlink deferral, ethos not installed) is the captured host status `$_host_status`: 0 when this runs standalone (git starts the hook with `$? = 0`), **or the host hook's fall-through status when this is chained after a foreign hook.**

And restated at `:44-49`, immediately above the assignment:

> Preserve a chained host hook's fall-through status. When install.sh appends this script after a foreign hook's content, `$?` here is that hook's last command status; returning it on passthrough keeps chaining from masking a host hook that signals failure by fall-through. **Standalone**, git invokes us fresh with `$? = 0`, so this is exit 0 as before. Captured before any command runs (a later assignment would reset `$?`).

So both branches are documented, in the right order, with the chained case — which is how it's actually installed in this repo — given the more detailed treatment. `"git starts the hook with $? = 0"` is scoped by "when this runs standalone" directly before it, not offered as the general case.

I'd rather say so than accept a correction that would make the comment redundant. You were right on the other two findings on this PR and I've filed both upstream; this one I'm reading as a scoping artifact of the quote rather than a defect in the text.
